1: Daniel and three friends are taken to serve at court. They refuse the king's food to keep God's law and thrive on vegetables and water.
Faithfulness in small things when far from home.
2: Nebuchadnezzar dreams of a statue of gold, silver, bronze and iron, shattered by a stone that becomes a mountain. Daniel explains: four kingdoms, then God's kingdom that lasts for ever.
Christ is the stone not cut by human hands.
3: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego refuse to worship a golden statue and are thrown into a furnace. A fourth figure walks with them, and they sing a hymn calling all creation to bless the Lord.
"Even if he does not save us, we will not serve your gods." The hymn is prayed in the Church's morning prayer.
4: Nebuchadnezzar dreams of a great tree cut down. He loses his reason and lives like an animal until he acknowledges that the Most High rules.
Pride is a kind of madness.
5: King Belshazzar drinks from the Temple vessels. A hand writes on the wall: weighed and found wanting. That night Babylon falls.
6: Jealous officials get prayer banned. Daniel keeps praying three times a day with his windows open and is thrown to the lions. An angel shuts their mouths.
Daniel changes nothing in his prayer under threat.
7: Four beasts and the Son of Man
Four beasts rise from the sea. The Ancient of Days takes his throne, and "one like a son of man" comes on the clouds and receives everlasting kingship.
Jesus takes his favourite title, Son of Man, from here.
8: A goat from the west breaks a two-horned ram; a small horn then attacks the sanctuary.
Persia, Greece, and a persecuting king, with an end set by God.
9: Daniel confesses the people's sins. Gabriel announces seventy weeks of years until an anointed one comes and is cut off.
Christians have read this of the coming and death of Christ.
10: After three weeks of fasting Daniel sees a dazzling man and is strengthened. The messenger had been delayed by a struggle with a heavenly "prince".
Prayer is heard from the first day, even when the answer is delayed.
11: A detailed forecast of wars between two dynasties, ending with a king who profanes the Temple and persecutes the faithful.
"The people who know their God shall stand firm."
12: Michael will arise. Many who sleep in the dust will awake, some to everlasting life, some to shame. The wise will shine like stars.
One of the clearest Old Testament statements of the resurrection.
13: Two elders try to force the virtuous Susanna and, refused, accuse her of adultery. Young Daniel questions them separately and exposes the lie.
Susanna chooses death over sin, and God defends the innocent.
14: Daniel shows with scattered ashes that priests, not the idol Bel, eat its food. He kills a serpent the Babylonians worship and survives the lions' den again.
Idols are exposed with a little common sense.
